title: Rhinoplasty guide Rhinoplasty: Appearance, Breathing and Recovery
excerpt: What to discuss about your goals, technique, swelling and healing, and why cosmetic and functional planning are assessed separately.
content:
Start with what bothers you, not a photo of someone else

A good rhinoplasty consultation begins with your own concern: a bump on the bridge, a wide or drooping tip, asymmetry after an injury, or difficulty breathing through one side. Describing the concern clearly helps the surgeon judge what can change while keeping the nose in balance with the rest of your face.

Reference photos can be useful to show a direction, but every face has different skin thickness, bone structure and proportions. The aim is a nose that suits you, not a copy of another person's profile.

Appearance and breathing are planned together

The shape of the nose and the way air flows through it are closely linked. Reducing or narrowing the nose without supporting its internal structure can affect breathing, so the airway is assessed as part of planning, even when the main goal is cosmetic. If you already have a blocked side, frequent congestion or a history of nasal injury, mention it early. Some functional problems can be addressed during the same procedure.

What recovery usually involves

Most people notice swelling and some bruising around the nose and eyes in the first days. Visible bruising settles first, while subtle swelling, especially at the tip, takes much longer to fade. The final shape develops gradually, so early results are not the end result. check_circle
  • Plan for a few days of rest and avoid strenuous activity until you are advised otherwise check_circle Follow instructions on sleeping position, splints and cleaning check_circle Protect the nose from knocks and avoid pressure from heavy glasses until cleared check_circle Attend follow-up visits so healing can be checked
When a non-surgical option may be discussed Small contour irregularities can sometimes be camouflaged with injectable fillers. This does not reduce the size of the nose or improve breathing, and it carries its own risks, so it is only suitable for selected concerns after a careful assessment.

title: Understanding Rhinoplasty Recovery: Week-by-Week Healing Guide
excerpt: A comprehensive clinical breakdown of what to expect during your rhinoplasty recovery journey, from cast removal to final nasal definition.

author.name: Dr. Sukhbir Singh
author.role: Senior Consultant Plastic & Cosmetic Surgeon, MS, M.Ch

content:
The Journey to Your Refined Profile

Rhinoplasty is widely considered one of the most artistically demanding and mathematically precise procedures in plastic surgery. While the surgery itself typically takes between 2 to 3.5 hours, the post-operative recovery plays a vital 50% role in achieving your final aesthetic and structural outcome.

At Resplendent Aesthetics in Greater Kailash, New Delhi, Dr. Sukhbir Singh utilizes advanced preservation rhinoplasty and structural grafting techniques designed to minimize tissue trauma and expedite healing.

Week 1: Cast and Initial Splint Phase

The first 7 days require the highest level of adherence to post-operative instructions:

  • Nasal Splint: A thermoplastic splint is worn continuously to stabilize the repositioned nasal bones and cartilages.
  • Head Elevation: Sleep with your head elevated at 30 to 45 degrees using 2-3 pillows to minimize edema.
  • Swelling & Bruising: Periorbital bruising peaks around Day 3 and begins clearing significantly by Day 6.
  • No Nose Blowing: Use saline nasal sprays as prescribed to keep internal passages clear without applying pressure.

Weeks 2 to 4: Return to Social Life

By day 7-8, the splint is removed in clinic. While initial swelling is visible, approximately 70% of noticeable swelling resolves by the end of the first month. Most patients comfortably return to non-strenuous desk jobs and social outings after 10-14 days.

"The secret to a natural rhinoplasty is structural harmony — respecting the patient's individual facial proportions rather than creating a generic shape."
— Dr. Sukhbir Singh

Months 2 to 12: Cartilage Settling & Tip Definition

Nasal tip skin is thicker than the dorsum and takes the longest to contract. By month 6, subtle contours emerge cleanly, and full micro-structural settling is complete at the 12-month mark.

Essential Tips for Expedited Healing

  1. Avoid wearing heavy eyeglasses resting directly on the bridge for 6 weeks.
  2. Refrain from strenuous cardio and heavy lifting for 3 to 4 weeks.
  3. Maintain a low-sodium diet and stay well hydrated.
  4. Protect the nose with SPF 50+ mineral sunscreen whenever outdoors.

title: FUE vs. DHI Hair Transplant: Which Technique Delivers the Densest Results?
excerpt: Compare Follicular Unit Extraction (FUE) and Direct Hair Implantation (DHI) to discover the ideal choice for hairline design, graft survival, and density.

author.name: Dr. Sukhbir Singh
author.role: Senior Consultant Plastic & Cosmetic Surgeon, MS, M.Ch

content:
Choosing the Right Hair Restoration Technique

Modern hair restoration has evolved far beyond the unnatural plugs of previous decades. Today, microscopic graft extraction and precision implantation allow surgeon-led clinics to achieve 100% natural, undetectable results.

When researching hair transplants in Delhi, patients frequently ask: What is the difference between FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction) and DHI (Direct Hair Implantation)?

Understanding FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction)

In standard FUE, individual follicular units containing 1 to 4 hairs are harvested from the safe donor zone at the back and sides of the scalp using specialized micro-punches (0.7mm–0.9mm). Tiny recipient incisions (channels) are then created at precise angles before inserting the grafts manually.

Advantages of FUE:

  • Ideal for large areas of baldness requiring 3,000 to 5,000+ grafts in a single or multi-day session.
  • Cost-effective with high graft viability when performed by an experienced plastic surgeon.
  • Minimal scarring with dot-like micro scars that are invisible under short hair.

Understanding DHI (Direct Hair Implantation)

DHI is a refined variation of FUE. While extraction is identical, implantation uses a specialized pen-like instrument (Choi Implanter). The implanter creates the incision and places the graft simultaneously in one fluid movement.

Key Advantages of DHI:

  • Maximum Depth & Angle Control: Unmatched precision for recreating delicate hairline transitions and temple peaks.
  • Reduced Out-of-Body Time: Grafts spend less time in holding solutions, maximizing graft survival rates above 95%.
  • Higher Density in Small Areas: Allows tighter packing of grafts without damaging surrounding existing hairs.

Summary: Which Is Right For You?

If you require high-density frontal hairline reconstruction or eyebrow restoration, DHI offers unmatched precision. For extensive crown and mid-scalp coverage requiring larger graft counts, FUE or a hybrid combination represents the clinical gold standard.

title: Facial Rejuvenation in Your 30s, 40s & 50s: Non-Surgical vs. Surgical Options
excerpt: A plastic surgeon's guide to age-appropriate facial aesthetics — from preventive Botox and dermal fillers to deep-plane face and neck lifts.

author.name: Dr. Sukhbir Singh
author.role: Senior Consultant Plastic & Cosmetic Surgeon, MS, M.Ch

content:
The Science of Natural Facial Aging

Facial aging is not just skin deep — it is a multi-layered anatomical process involving volume loss in deep fat pads, weakening of the SMAS (Superficial Musculoaponeurotic System), bone resorption around the orbits and jawline, and decreased collagen synthesis.

A personalized facial rejuvenation strategy targets the specific anatomical changes occurring at each decade of life.

Your 30s: Prevention & Subtle Enhancement

In your 30s, dynamic expression lines begin settling into static wrinkles, and initial midface fat depletion may create slight under-eye hollows.

  • Preventive Botox: Softens forehead lines, glabellar frown lines, and crow's feet.
  • Hyaluronic Acid Micro-Fillers: Subtle tear-trough correction and cheek support to maintain youthful light reflection.
  • HydraFacial & Medical Peels: Deep pore cleansing and cellular turnover.

Your 40s: Restoring Midface Volume & Jawline Definition

By the 40s, ligament laxity leads to early jowl formation and deepening of nasolabial folds.

  • Structural Dermal Fillers: Volumizing the zygomatic arch and angle of the mandible to lift sagging tissue.
  • Blepharoplasty (Eyelid Surgery): Removing heavy upper lid skin or lower eye bags for an alert, refreshed appearance.
  • Thread Lifts & Laser Skin Tightening: Collagen stimulation for mild tissue laxity.

Your 50s and Beyond: Deep Plane Surgical Restoration

When significant skin excess and platysma muscle bands develop along the neck, non-surgical treatments alone cannot provide a youthful neckline without looking overfilled.

  • Face & Neck Lift: Repositioning the deeper SMAS layer rather than just pulling skin tight, restoring a crisp, elegant jawline.
  • Autologous Fat Grafting: Transferring micro-purified fat to restore natural facial volume permanently.
